audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Volibear all seven rows, including the two rows whose own why-lines say the lane evens out and then goes to Cho'Gath.
audit.why: The already-audited chogath__volibear mirror sets the chart to Skill / Volibear / Volibear / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath with ratings 5,4,4,6,7,7,7 from his side. Ours must be the inverse, or mirror-fix.js overwrites it.
audit.corrected: Row 0 Skill, rows 1-2 Volibear, rows 3-6 Cho'Gath; ratings 5,6,6,4,3,3,3. Proposed as matched full/content pairs with every affected why rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags zero sequencing cues — no cooldown appeared anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: The whole lane turns on when Feral Scream and Feast are available.
audit.corrected: Rupture 6s / 950 range, Feral Scream 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s at 300 range, Feast 80/70/60s at 175 range, Stormbringer 160s and Frenzied Maul 5s written into early, mid, late, all four spikes and the phase whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Vorpal Spikes was labelled his W and also called 'his passive'; the silence's real effect on Volibear's pattern was never stated.
audit.why: Vorpal Spikes is E (released by his attacks); W is Feral Scream, a 300-range cone silence. Silence is the decisive interaction: it denies Frenzied Maul's second cast, the Sky Splitter shield and the Stormbringer cast. Rupture's knockup ends the Thundering Smash approach before the stun lands, because the stun rides his first attack. And Stormbringer disables YOUR tower on landing, so it is not an escape.
audit.corrected: Written into spikes[0-3], early, mid, late, whys[1], whys[3], whys[4], whys[5], wants.you[1], wants.foe[2] and phases[3-6].why.

audit.why: The passive is The Relentless Storm.

edits.before: W ranks make the wounded-bite chunk hard. Run Cho'Gath down every time Rupture (Knockup) is on cooldown — you win the stat-check from here to 6.
edits.after: Feral Scream (11s at rank 1, 300-range cone) silences you mid-pattern — no Frenzied Maul second bite, no Sky Splitter shield, no trade.

edits.before: Stormbringer online — you can dive Cho'Gath under tower with the disable. The 3-6 window is the strongest your lane will ever be: cash it.
edits.after: Feast (80s) is 175-range true damage that ignores your health stacking, and Stormbringer disables your own tower on the way out.

edits.before: Sundered Sky doubles down on the all-in: crit-heal on the first hit of every fight. Force Cho'Gath to fight or lose the wave.
edits.after: His first Feast stacks turn the wave against you: every devoured minion is permanent health you now have to chew through.

edits.before: With two items you're a drain-tank Cho'Gath can't burst. Only discipline beats you now — never int the Q stun into ready CC and the lane stays yours.
edits.after: Two items in he is a wall: Feral Scream cancels your Stormbringer cast and Feast's true damage ignores everything you built. Dive past him.

edits.before: At level 2 your second ability and Relentless Storm ramp out-trade his single-target poke.
edits.after: At level 2 Frenzied Maul's 5s second bite and The Relentless Storm out-trade his poke.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 your DPS and slow still beat his pre-Feast sustain in extended trades.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 go to him — Feral Scream (11s) silences you out of the trade entirely.

edits.before: At 6 your Stormbringer engage out-threatens him before Feast is stacked enough to matter.
edits.after: At 6 Feast's true damage beats the Stormbringer dive, and your tower is disabled too.

edits.before: By first item it evens out as his Feast stacks and poke let him trade back.
edits.after: By first item he is ahead: Feast stacks turn every trade into his health pool.

edits.before: With all three basics you can Q-flurry Cho'Gath's Rupture (Q) delay: sidestep the ground-crack, W his passive Vorpal Spikes off cooldown, and your Relentless Storm stacks out-DPS his sustain before he has meaningful tankiness.
edits.after: Rupture (6s, 950 range) has a delay you can walk out of — its knockup is what ends your Thundering Smash approach before the stun lands. Sidestep it, then Frenzied Maul twice on the mark while The Relentless Storm ramps.

edits.before: Stormbringer lets you leap onto him and E-slow his escape, but this is where Cho'Gath's own R Feast comes online — respect the true-damage execute if you're low, since a landed Feast on you is 20+ permanent HP for him.
edits.after: Stormbringer (160s) leaps and disables his tower, but Feast (80s) is true damage at 175 range and Feral Scream silences the cast outright — do not open the dive into a ready scream, or the leap never happens.

edits.before: Around first item it evens out: your Sheen/bramble spike is real but Cho'Gath's first Feast stacks plus his Q/W poke start letting him trade back and shove you off the wave.
edits.after: By first item he is ahead: Feast stacks are permanent max health, and Carnivore restores health and mana on every kill, so he never has to leave the wave.

edits.before: Late the Feast stacks and Silence (W) turn him into an unkillable frontline that shuts down your R re-cast; you win skirmishes only by diving his carries, not by dueling him.
edits.after: Late, Feast stacks and Feral Scream's silence turn him into a wall — the scream denies your Stormbringer cast and your Sky Splitter shield. Dive his carries, never duel him.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are even — Cho'Gath's Rupture (Q) and Vorpal Spikes (W) out-range your melee poke, but neither of you commits, so it comes down to dodging his Q telegraph.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are even — Rupture (950 range) and Vorpal Spikes (his E, off his attacks) out-range you, but neither commits, so it comes down to dodging the ground-crack.

edits.before: Once you have your full kit you're ahead: chain Q-stun into W-maul and your passive lightning shreds him before Feast gives real tankiness, and your E slow punishes his slow, low-range escape.
edits.after: Levels 2-3 are your window: Thundering Smash stuns on your first attack and Frenzied Maul's second bite on the same mark heals you. From 4 on, Feral Scream (11s) silences that pattern before it finishes.

edits.before: After first item and into Feast stacks the matchup flips — his silence, sustain, and true-damage execute make him a brick you can't kill, so pivot to peeling and diving past him.
edits.after: From first item on, Feast stacks and Feral Scream make him a brick you cannot kill — the silence eats your Stormbringer cast. Pivot to peeling and diving past him.

edits.before: Stack Relentless Storm early and all-in before Feast stacks
edits.after: Stack The Relentless Storm and all-in before Feast grows

edits.before: Silence (W) you mid-R to cancel your leap engage
edits.after: Feral Scream you mid-cast to cancel Stormbringer
